tagline: Leading regional property and casualty insurer with strong capital management and regulatory compliance
hero_kpi_rationale: Key revenue indicator for a P&C insurer, reflecting the company's ability to generate $5.7 billion in premiums while maintaining solvency above 350% of required RBC ratio

kpis.name: Net Premiums Written
kpis.explanation: Total net premiums written by the insurance company for the year
kpis.description: Net premiums written represent the total volume of insurance business written by the company, a key revenue metric for property and casualty insurers

kpis.name: Risk-Based Capital Ratio
kpis.explanation: Percentage of regulatory capital held relative to authorized control level, key solvency measure for insurers
kpis.description: The RBC Ratio is a regulatory measure that captures varying elements of risks undertaken by insurance writers. A ratio of 200% or less would require regulatory action. Mercury General maintains a ratio of 350% or greater.
kpis.signal: Strong solvency position well above regulatory minimums

kpis.name: Premiums to Surplus Ratio
kpis.explanation: Ratio of premium volume written to policyholder surplus, indicator of underwriting capacity
kpis.description: Industry guidelines suggest this ratio should not exceed 3.0 to 1. Mercury General's ratio of 2.39 to 1, based on $5.7B net premiums written and $2.39B combined surplus, demonstrates conservative capital management.
kpis.signal: Prudent underwriting capacity well within industry guidelines

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The Board considers cybersecurity risk as critical to the enterprise with full Board oversight through the Enterprise Risk Management program. Regular independent third-party technology assessments are conducted, and the CEO provides Information Security Incident Reports to the Board. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Regulatory Changes
risks.score_rationale: The company operates under strict insurance regulations, particularly in California. Recent regulations (late 2024) on catastrophe modeling and reinsurance cost incorporation impact pricing and market share requirements effective July 2026. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Catastrophe Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company is highly exposed to catastrophe risks including hurricanes, wildfires, fires, and earthquakes. The January 2025 Palisades and Eaton wildfires resulted in a $50 million California FAIR Plan assessment. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive market where larger competitors with greater financial resources may impact market share and profitability. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Climate Change
risks.score_rationale: The company faces increasing exposure to climate-related risks through higher frequency and severity of natural catastrophes, particularly wildfires and weather-related events in its primary markets. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Interest Rate Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company invests substantially in interest-sensitive assets, with 82.5% of total investments in fixed maturity securities. Interest rate changes directly impact portfolio value and reinvestment income. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Litigation Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company faces potential litigation exposure inherent in insurance operations, though recent market conduct examinations have not identified material findings. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Reputational Risk
risks.score_rationale: Reputation issues in insurance operations could impact the company's ability to attract and retain customers, particularly during catastrophic events or market conduct examination issues. (default score, to be refined)
